+/// Gives every producer in the plan a name of its own.
+/// A producer registers its channels under its name and each consumer takes one of them
+/// by that name. One bound subquery can occur twice in a plan, e.g. behind a SELECT alias
+/// that is referenced again, or as an argument that a SQL function uses twice. Both copies
+/// then produce their CTEs under the same names: the later producer replaces the channels
+/// of the earlier one, and the consumers of both copies are counted together.
+/// The consumers of a producer are on the right side of its `Sequence`, so a renamed
+/// producer takes the consumers there with it. A later name keeps the display name, which
+/// `scopes` maps the name of each enclosing producer to the name it now has.
+/// Sets each producer's `ref_count` to the number of consumers left in the physical plan.
+/// The producer opens one channel per counted consumer and sends every block to each of
+/// them, while each consumer takes one channel when its pipeline is built. The logical
+/// count can be too high: physical building may drop a consumer, e.g. an aggregate with
+/// no keys and no used functions becomes a `ConstantTableScan` and its input, a
+/// consumer, is never built. Nobody reads that extra channel, so a bounded one fills up
+/// and blocks the producer and every other consumer.
+    fn sequence(left: PhysicalPlan, right: PhysicalPlan) -> PhysicalPlan {
+        // x and y read the base CTE; a second x, nested in the first one's scope, has a
+        // consumer of its own. `__materialized_cte_0_x` is already taken.
+        // The steps build their pipelines when they run, and only then do the materialized
+        // CTE consumers in them take their channels.
+        // Every fragment of the query on this node is built, and a consumer takes its
+        // channel while its fragment is built.
+    /// Marks materialized CTEs whose consumers are built after the query pipeline: the
+    /// recursive CTE source builds the pipelines of its steps when they run.

+# A CTE read twice is materialized through channels. Here one reader is in the seed of
+# a recursive CTE, which builds its pipeline only when the recursive CTE runs, after
+WITH m AS (SELECT number AS n FROM numbers(5))
+    WITH RECURSIVE r AS (SELECT max(n) AS x FROM m UNION ALL SELECT x - 1 FROM r WHERE x > 0)
+# Grouping sets whose outer query reads only some of their columns. The UNION
+# rewrites feed each grouping level from a CTE that sends every block to each of
+# its readers through a small bounded channel. Physical planning can drop a
+# reader: a level with no keys and no used aggregate becomes a constant scan and
+# no longer reads the level it was derived from. A channel left for a dropped
+# reader fills up and the query hangs, so the queries here make the producing
+# level send more blocks than the channel holds: keys have up to 40 values and
+# blocks hold 4 rows. A few cases keep every reader and guard the results.
+# Readers are also lost when two copies of one subquery share CTE names. Run
+# with the default cascading UNION rewrite, the plain UNION rewrite, the
+# cascading rewrite without the hierarchical rule, and native expansion, which
+# Three inserts give a cluster several blocks to distribute.
+CREATE TABLE t(p INT NOT NULL, a INT NOT NULL, b INT NULL, v INT NOT NULL)
+INSERT INTO t SELECT number % 40, number % 3, if(number % 7 = 0, NULL, number % 5), number
+INSERT INTO t SELECT number % 40, number % 3, if(number % 7 = 0, NULL, number % 5), number
+INSERT INTO t SELECT number % 40, number % 3, if(number % 7 = 0, NULL, number % 5), number
+# The grand total of each form becomes a constant scan.
+FROM (SELECT p, a, sum(v) AS s FROM t GROUP BY CUBE(p, a)) x
+FROM (SELECT p, a, b, sum(v) AS s FROM t GROUP BY ROLLUP(p, a, b)) x
+FROM (SELECT p, a, b, max(v) AS m FROM t GROUP BY CUBE(p, a, b)) x
+# AVG makes the UNION rewrite fall back from the hierarchical form, so every
+# set reads the same input CTE.
+FROM (SELECT p, a, avg(v) AS m FROM t GROUP BY GROUPING SETS ((p), (a), ())) x
+FROM (SELECT p, a, sum(v) AS s FROM t GROUP BY GROUPING SETS ((p, a), (p), (p), (), ())) x
+# A plain key next to a CUBE leaves no empty set, so no level becomes a constant
+# scan and every reader is kept.
+FROM (SELECT p, a, sum(v) AS s FROM t GROUP BY p, CUBE(a)) x
+# grouping() is computed per set, not read from the input.
+FROM (SELECT p, grouping(p, a) AS g, sum(v) AS s FROM t GROUP BY CUBE(p, a)) x
+# Counting the output rows reads no column at all.
+SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT p, a, sum(v) AS s FROM t GROUP BY CUBE(p, a)) x
+# The grand total keeps the used aggregate and still reads its input.
+FROM (SELECT p, a, sum(v) AS s1, count(*) AS c, max(v) AS m FROM t GROUP BY CUBE(p, a)) x
+## Consumers that stop early or sit under other operators
+# LIMIT stops the outer query before every level is read.
+    SELECT p FROM (SELECT p, a, sum(v) AS s FROM t GROUP BY CUBE(p, a)) x LIMIT 5
+SELECT p, a FROM (SELECT p, a, sum(v) AS s FROM t GROUP BY CUBE(p, a)) x
+ORDER BY p NULLS FIRST, a NULLS FIRST LIMIT 3
+    SELECT p, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY a ORDER BY p) AS rn
+    FROM (SELECT p, a, sum(v) AS s FROM t GROUP BY CUBE(p, a)) x
+FROM (SELECT p, a, sum(v) AS s FROM t GROUP BY CUBE(p, a)) x
+SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT DISTINCT p FROM (SELECT p, a, sum(v) AS s FROM t GROUP BY CUBE(p, a)) x)
+## Grouping sets in subqueries and set operations
+WHERE p IN (SELECT p FROM (SELECT p, a, sum(v) AS s FROM t GROUP BY CUBE(p, a)) x WHERE a IS NULL)
+WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM (SELECT p, a, sum(v) AS s FROM t GROUP BY CUBE(p, a)) x WHERE x.p = t.p)
+SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT p, a, sum(v) AS s FROM t GROUP BY CUBE(p, a)) x)
+# Two independent chains under one UNION ALL.
+    SELECT p, a, sum(v) AS s FROM t GROUP BY CUBE(p, a)
+    SELECT p, a, sum(v) AS s FROM t GROUP BY ROLLUP(p, a)
+# A CTE inlined at both references, each reading only its keys.
+WITH x AS (SELECT p, a, sum(v) AS s FROM t GROUP BY CUBE(p, a))
+SELECT count(*), count(x1.p) FROM x x1 JOIN x x2 ON x1.p = x2.p AND x1.a = x2.a
+WITH x AS MATERIALIZED (SELECT p, a, sum(v) AS s FROM t GROUP BY CUBE(p, a))
+# Referencing the alias of a scalar subquery again copies the bound subquery, so
+# both copies rewrite to CTEs derived from the same expression. Each copy needs
+SELECT (SELECT sum(s) FROM (SELECT p, a, sum(v) AS s FROM t GROUP BY CUBE(p, a)) x) AS c1, c1 + 1
+    SELECT p, (SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT p, sum(v) AS s FROM t GROUP BY ROLLUP(p)) x) AS c
+# INSERT and CREATE TABLE AS plan their SELECT the same way.
+CREATE TABLE keys(p INT NULL, a INT NULL)
+INSERT INTO keys SELECT p, a FROM (SELECT p, a, sum(v) AS s FROM t GROUP BY CUBE(p, a)) x
+CREATE TABLE keys_ctas AS SELECT p, a FROM (SELECT p, a, sum(v) AS s FROM t GROUP BY ROLLUP(p, a)) x
+SELECT count(*), count(p), count(a), (SELECT count(*) FROM keys_ctas) FROM keys
+## Grouping sets over inputs that run on one node
+CREATE TABLE d(p INT NOT NULL, name STRING NOT NULL)
+INSERT INTO d SELECT number, concat('n', number::STRING) FROM numbers(20)
+INSERT INTO d SELECT number, concat('n', number::STRING) FROM numbers(40) WHERE number >= 20
+# A sorted LIMIT runs on one node. On a cluster, the CTE over its rows is

+FROM (SELECT p, a, sum(v) AS s FROM (SELECT * FROM t ORDER BY v LIMIT 900) z GROUP BY CUBE(p, a)) x
+    (SELECT p, a, sum(v) AS s FROM t GROUP BY CUBE(p, a) ORDER BY s LIMIT 30)
+    (SELECT p, b, sum(v) AS s FROM t GROUP BY ROLLUP(p, b) ORDER BY s DESC LIMIT 30)
+    SELECT p, a, max(rn) AS m
+    FROM (SELECT p, a, v, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY p ORDER BY v) AS rn FROM t) z
+## Readers under joins, windows and correlated subqueries
+# A window without PARTITION BY reads every level on one node.
+    SELECT p, a, s, row_number() OVER (ORDER BY s, p, a) AS rn
+    FROM (SELECT p, a, sum(v) AS s FROM t GROUP BY CUBE(p, a)) x
+# So does a full join on a non-equal condition.
+SELECT count(*), sum(s) FROM (SELECT p, a, sum(v) AS s FROM t GROUP BY CUBE(p, a)) x FULL JOIN d ON x.p > d.p
+FROM t JOIN (SELECT p, a, sum(v) AS s FROM t GROUP BY CUBE(p, a)) x ON t.p = x.p AND t.a = x.a
+FROM t JOIN (SELECT p, a, sum(v) AS s FROM t GROUP BY CUBE(p, a)) x ON t.p = x.p AND t.a = x.a
+# Both sides of the join read grouping sets, from two chains.
+FROM (SELECT p, a, sum(v) AS s FROM t GROUP BY CUBE(p, a)) x
+JOIN (SELECT p, b, sum(v) AS s FROM t GROUP BY ROLLUP(p, b)) y ON x.p = y.p
+FROM (SELECT p, a, sum(v) AS s FROM t GROUP BY CUBE(p, a)) x
+JOIN (SELECT p, a, sum(v) AS s FROM t GROUP BY CUBE(p, a)) y ON x.p = y.p AND x.a = y.a
